entries.title: Functional Medicine Lab Interpretation & Analysis
entries.pitch: Master comprehensive lab panel interpretation across thyroid, metabolic, inflammatory, and hormonal markers—the clinical foundation NPs need to assess root causes and design personalized treatment plans.
facts: Teaches interpretation of complete thyroid panel including TSH, Free T4, Free T3, and Reverse T3 to identify subclinical and clinical thyroid dysfunction.
Covers metabolic markers: homocysteine, uric acid, fasting insulin, glucose, and triglyceride/HDL ratio for cardiovascular and metabolic risk assessment.
Trains analysis of inflammatory biomarkers including high-sensitivity CRP and white blood cell count as indicators of systemic inflammation.
Addresses iron metabolism assessment through ferritin, serum iron, and iron saturation percentage for anemia and iron overload detection.
Includes micronutrient status evaluation: B12, Vitamin D, and electrolyte balance (sodium/potassium) critical for cellular function.
Teaches hepatic function interpretation via liver enzymes (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase) to screen for metabolic syndrome and toxin burden.
Covers sex hormone and adrenal assessment including estrogen, progesterone, testosterone, and DHEA-S to address hormonal imbalances.
Provides structured worksheets for multi-patient case tracking and longitudinal lab value monitoring to demonstrate clinical progression.
Trains NPs to recognize functional ranges—not just normal lab ranges—enabling earlier detection of subclinical disease patterns.
Enables evidence-based patient assessment that justifies functional medicine interventions and builds credibility with clients.
Supports practitioner ability to order, interpret, and track labs independently—a cornerstone of the functional medicine business model.

entries.title: Advanced Gut Health Case Studies: Multi-System Root Cause Analysis
entries.pitch: Learn how to connect gastrointestinal pathology to cardiac, dermatological, and gynecological symptoms using functional medicine frameworks and stool panel interpretation.
facts: Teaches interpretation of comprehensive stool analysis panels including bacterial pathogens, parasites, H. pylori virulence factors, dysbiosis markers, pancreatic enzyme sufficiency, and inflammatory biomarkers like calprotectin and secretory IgA.
Covers the clinical reasoning to connect low DAO enzyme production (declining progesterone in menopause) to histamine intolerance and its systemic manifestations across multiple organ systems.
Demonstrates how to identify when common health practices (fermented foods, probiotics) may be contraindicated based on individual biochemistry and microbiome status.
Includes case-based teaching on differential diagnosis: recognizing when a rash is histamine-driven rather than infectious (shingles) despite prior specialist labeling.

Teaches targeted supplementation protocols addressing root causes: H. pylori eradication, giardia and bacterial overgrowth treatment, microbiome restoration, and organ-system support (liver, pancreas, neurotransmitter synthesis).
Addresses how to manage patient expectations and monitor for herxheimer reactions during pathogen elimination and detoxification phases.
Covers hormonal-gut-microbiome axis: how sex hormone decline affects enzyme capacity and manifests as infections, rashes, and arrhythmias.
Demonstrates clinical outcome tracking: symptom resolution from cardiac arrhythmia, dyspnea, fatigue, and vaginal infections through gut-focused functional medicine intervention.
Teaches interpretation of supporting labs: CBC eosinophil/basophil trends, ferritin, iodine, thyroid panel, and hs-CRP in the context of gut dysbiosis and histamine burden.
Includes nutritional and botanical intervention frameworks: timing, dosing rationale, and sequencing of treatments to avoid GI upset and support detoxification pathways.

entries.title: Foundational Functional Medicine Case Studies Module
entries.pitch: Learn to recognize hidden root causes—environmental triggers, microbiome dysfunction, chronic stress patterns—by working through real-world cases that conventional medicine missed.
facts: Teaches clinical reasoning to connect symptom onset timing with environmental exposures (renovation materials, indoor air quality, home office hazards).
Covers how to identify when acute presentations mask chronic systemic issues requiring root-cause investigation beyond symptomatic treatment.
Demonstrates assessment of medication burden and iatrogenic effects (prednisone weight gain, NSAID overuse) in functional medicine context.
Includes analysis of psychosocial stressors (financial pressure, sleep disruption, anxiety rumination) as measurable drivers of inflammatory and pain conditions.
Teaches interpretation of symptom patterns (morning stiffness, time-of-day variation, exercise response) to guide differential diagnostic thinking.
Shows how to recognize antibiotic history and microbiome disruption as foundational factors in autoimmune-adjacent presentations.
Covers lifestyle factor assessment: exercise capacity, diet quality, sleep architecture, smoking status, social support as integrated clinical data.
Demonstrates case-building methodology that integrates timeline analysis, occupational/environmental history, medication timeline, and stress markers.
Teaches the functional medicine model of distinguishing between symptom relief (conventional outcome) and functional restoration (FM outcome).
Includes multi-system pattern recognition: respiratory + GI + musculoskeletal + neuroendocrine connections in single-patient narratives.

entries.title: Functional Medicine Chronic Case Studies: Cardiometabolic & Multi-System Disease
entries.pitch: Learn how to identify and treat root causes of chronic fatigue, metabolic dysfunction, and multi-system disease through real cases where standard labs missed diagnoses that FMP-C testing protocols reveal.
facts: Teaches comprehensive lab interpretation including thyroid panel, HPAT axis dysfunction markers, nutrient deficiency testing (vitamin D, magnesium, B vitamins), and gut permeability indicators.
Covers the 5R gut-healing protocol (Remove, Replace, Reinoculate, Repair, Retain) applied to IBS, leaky gut, and gluten sensitivity cases.
Trains practitioners to recognize insulin resistance via fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HgbA1c, and 2-hour glucose/insulin testing, including prediabetic range interpretation.
Addresses H. pylori infection discovery and treatment sequencing in cases presenting with chronic hives, platelet dysfunction, and lipid abnormalities.
Teaches advanced cardiometabolic panels: triglycerides, HDL/LDL, HS-CRP, fibrinogen, homocysteine, and LDL particle number for cardiovascular risk stratification.
Covers hormone testing and replacement strategy including testosterone deficiency and B12 status in aging male fatigue cases.
Demonstrates dietary intervention frameworks (elimination of grains, sugar, alcohol, gluten) paired with supplement protocols (omega-3, curcumin, berberine, digestive enzymes, probiotics).
Teaches stress-driven neuroendocrine dysfunction: how chronic stress impairs HPAT axis and thyroid function independent of TSH normality.
Includes case-study format showing multi-month outcome tracking: weight loss, inflammation markers, cognitive improvement, sexual function, and medication discontinuation.
Addresses cash-pay vs. insurance-reimbursement practice model decision-making and patient compliance challenges with prescription vs. supplement-based treatment.
Trains NPs to recognize when conventional "normal" lab ranges mask functional medicine pathology in exhaustion, brain fog, and metabolic failure cases.
Teaches integration of lifestyle coaching (meal prep, stress reduction, sleep, exercise restructuring) with pharmaceutical and supplement intervention sequencing.

entries.title: Estrogen & Progesterone Management in Functional Medicine
entries.pitch: Master sex hormone physiology, estrogen dominance recognition, and evidence-based BHRT prescribing to address fertility, menopause, PMS, and metabolic dysfunction in your NP practice.
facts: Teaches steroid hormone biosynthesis from cholesterol through pregnenolone, including cytochrome P450 enzymatic pathways and tissue-specific production sites (ovaries, adrenal, breast tissue, adipose storage).
Covers all four estrogen forms (estrone/E1, estradiol/E2, estriol/E3, estetrol/E4) and their distinct physiological roles in bone, cardiovascular, cognitive, and sexual health.

Provides lab interpretation protocols: estradiol optimal ranges by life stage (40–50 pg/mL for menopause, day-3 timing for fertility, day-21 for most presentations), DUTCH vs. serum cost-benefit analysis, and follow-up frequency (Q3–6 months).

Teaches estrogen dominance syndrome recognition: 15+ associated symptoms (heavy menstruation, mood swings, weight gain, anxiety, low ferritin/magnesium) and 9+ lab correlates (elevated CRP/insulin, low vitamin D/protein).
Addresses estrogen dominance conditions: PCOS, endometriosis, PMS/PMDD, infertility, insulin resistance, tumors, and medication-induced elevation (ampicillin, steroids, phenothiazines).
Prescribing framework: micronized progesterone dosing, cycling strategies for intact uterus, and symptom-guided titration with 6–8 week reassessment windows.
Teaches insulin-inflammation pathways: how carbohydrate consumption triggers insulin-mediated inflammation and hormone imbalance, linking grain consumption to phytate-blocking of iron/T3 absorption.
Includes adjunctive supplement and medication protocols: inositol, berberine/metformin, spironolactone, resveratrol, and curcumin with dose ranges and indications.
Covers fertility-specific management: micronized progesterone vs. synthetic progestins, AMH testing, cycle-day-specific lab draws, and progesterone's role in ovulation and pregnancy support.

Provides menopausal and menorrhagia follow-up frameworks: symptom diaries, comprehensive lab panels (CMP, ferritin, homocysteine, uric acid, CRP), and diagnosis coding (low/high estrogen, menopausal symptoms, menorrhagia).

Teaches evidence-based safety monitoring: annual or per-visit symptom questionnaires, red-flag lab changes requiring evaluation, mammography/ultrasound frequency based on risk, and when to stop hormone 3–4 days pre-draw for trough vs. peak levels.

Addresses progesterone's oppositional role as 'brakes' to estrogen/testosterone 'gas pedals' and its therapeutic uses in irregular cycles, endometrial hyperplasia, hot flashes, anxiety, and infertility support.

entries.title: Practice Integration and Business Considerations for Functional Medicine NPs
entries.pitch: Learn how to operationalize functional medicine in your practice, manage lab relationships for profitability, and document patient education on non-FDA labs to build a revenue-generating FM business.
facts: Teaches negotiation strategies with lab vendors and pricing models (2-4x markup rule for cash-based labs).
Covers documentation best practices for functional medicine visits, including patient education on risks/benefits of non-FDA labs.
Provides vetted lab partner relationships: Access Medical Labs, Rupa Health, and Genova Diagnostics with discounted pricing frameworks.
Clarifies regulatory requirements (no CLIA waiver needed to draw labs in-practice) to reduce compliance barriers.
Instructs on establishing your practice as primary care provider or transitioning patients to PCP relationships in a functional medicine model.
Teaches how to position functional medicine as a high-demand, top-5% competency market differentiator for NPs.
Covers patient education protocols tailored to both patient and parent (when applicable) for non-standard diagnostic tools.
Addresses alternative diagnostic and treatment option discussions as documentation and informed consent strategy.
Teaches lab ordering competency across serum, allergy, and specialized functional panels integrated into practice workflow.
Explains functional medicine's role as a revenue-generating service line and business model for NP-owned or employed practices.

entries.title: Advanced Functional and Laboratory Testing Course
entries.pitch: Master ordering and interpreting 50+ advanced lab panels to identify root causes of chronic disease and differentiate yourself in functional medicine practice.
facts: Teaches interpretation of organic acid testing, mycotoxin, gut microbiome, IgG food sensitivity, and heavy metal/environmental toxin panels.
Covers advanced reading of standard labs including CBC, CMP, NMR lipid panel, PSA, omega-3/6 ratios, and lipid particle analysis (Pattern A vs. B LDL).
Includes deep-dive into oxidized LDL, apolipoprotein B, and cardiovascular risk markers beyond conventional cholesterol interpretation.
Teaches DUTCH test (hormonal metabolites) interpretation with detailed case studies and clinical application frameworks.
Over 14 hours of content with dozens of lab panels, covering when to order, what results mean, and how to use findings in patient care.
Provides comprehensive functional vs. conventional lab reference ranges and initial lab recommendation bundles (iron panel, thyroid full cascade, inflammatory markers, nutrient status).
Integrates lifestyle and dietary approaches aligned with lab findings (detoxification support, microbiome restoration, anti-inflammatory foods).
Designed for any NP specialty (HRT, weight loss, primary care) with immediate practice integration regardless of setting or resources.
Taught by experienced clinician-owners: Justin Allan (FNP, Elite NP), Dr. Brendan Tennefoss (DNP telehealth), Justin Groce (functional clinic owner).
Positions NPs in top 5% of clinical competence in functional lab interpretation, addressing patient demand for advanced testing knowledge.
Includes real patient case studies with full lab panels and clinical decision-making workups.
Assumes foundational functional medicine knowledge but accessible to those with integrative medicine training seeking advanced lab skills.

entries.title: Advanced Functional Case Studies and Laboratory Testing Part 1
entries.pitch: Learn to interpret comprehensive lab panels through a real 33-year-old case with fatigue, GI dysfunction, and sleep disturbance—mastering the functional medicine differential diagnostic approach NPs need to identify root causes others miss.
facts: Teaches interpretation of complete metabolic panels (CMP), lipid ratios (TC/HDL, LDL/HDL, TG/HDL), and CBC differentials beyond reference ranges to detect early metabolic dysfunction and immune suppression.

Covers functional vs. conventional lab reading: identifies subtle trends (e.g., rising glucose 4.9→5.4 A1C, elevated BUN/creatinine ratio) that suggest dehydration, protein dysmetabolism, or renal changes before clinical disease.

Trains assessment of hormonal markers including salivary cortisol patterns (4-point diurnal curve), fasting insulin, TSH, testosterone, and vitamin D to map HPA axis dysregulation and adrenal insufficiency.
Teaches candida immune complex and hs-CRP interpretation to differentiate gut dysbiosis, fungal overgrowth, and low-grade inflammation from autoimmune or systemic inflammatory conditions.

Addresses nutritional biomarker analysis: albumin/globulin ratios, liver enzyme patterns (ALT/AST/GGT/ALP), and implications for protein status, immune suppression, and potential nutrient deficiencies (B6, zinc, magnesium, CoQ10).

Presents functional medicine differential diagnoses framework: dysbiosis, leaky gut, mitochondrial dysfunction, adrenal fatigue, histamine intolerance, oxalate sensitivity, hypochlorhydria—each mapped to lab findings and symptom clusters.

Demonstrates how to correlate conventional labs with dietary history, medication use (sertraline, cyclobenzaprine), supplement protocols, and food sensitivities to build integrated root-cause hypotheses.

Teaches differential reasoning for complex presentations: distinguishes between primary liver/bone disease, metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular risk, and secondary gut-driven cholesterol dysregulation.
Covers case-based integration of sleep study findings (mild obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy concerns) with lab markers (elevated RBC, hemoglobin) to identify fatigue contributors.

Trains recognition of iatrogenic patterns: how prior antimicrobials (tetracycline, metronidazole, rifaximin) and restrictive diets (vegan→carnivore→paleo) shape microbiome, nutrient status, and immune tolerance.

Teaches interpretation of prior negative conventional workups (colonoscopy, standard stool analysis, autoimmune panels) alongside positive functional findings to frame the functional medicine value proposition.
Includes assessment of supplement tolerance, IgG immunoglobulin reactions, and food-specific immune responses to guide safe therapeutic sequencing in patients with severe intestinal permeability.

entries.title: Functional Vitamin, Supplement & Nutrition Case Study Analysis
entries.pitch: Learn to interpret comprehensive micronutrient and metabolic lab panels to identify hidden deficiencies and metabolic dysfunction driving fatigue, brain fog, and hormonal symptoms in perimenopausal women.
facts: Teaches interpretation of complete thyroid function panels including TSH, FT4, FT3, and reverse T3 to assess thyroid adequacy beyond standard dosing.
Covers micronutrient assessment via vitamin D, B12, iron panel, ferritin, and iron saturation to identify deficiencies contributing to fatigue and cognitive dysfunction.
Addresses electrolyte and protein status interpretation (sodium, potassium, total protein, albumin, globulin) as nutritional markers of systemic health.
Includes metabolic dysfunction assessment through fasting insulin, glucose, and A1c to identify insulin resistance and prediabetic states.
Teaches analysis of inflammatory markers (CRP-hs) and metabolic byproducts (homocysteine, uric acid) linked to chronic symptom patterns.
Covers hormone assessment in perimenopausal transitions, including estradiol, estrone, and testosterone evaluation for symptom causation.
Uses real-world case studies of symptomatic patients with multiple lab abnormalities to teach pattern recognition across systems.
Demonstrates how to prioritize supplement and nutritional interventions based on lab findings rather than symptom-driven guessing.
Teaches CBC (white blood cells, red blood cells) interpretation within functional medicine context.
Includes liver function enzyme assessment (alkaline phosphatase, AST, ALT) to evaluate nutritional metabolism capacity.
Addresses the relationship between thyroid medication adequacy, nutrient absorption, and persistent symptoms despite 'normal' TSH.
Integrates case-based learning where practitioners analyze multi-system dysfunction to recommend targeted supplementation strategies.

entries.title: Functional Vitamins, Supplements & Nutrition Course
entries.pitch: Learn evidence-based supplement and nutritional assessment, interpretation, and recommendation strategies to add a high-margin revenue service that patients actively seek from licensed providers.
facts: Teaches interpretation of functional vs. normal reference ranges for micronutrient lab panels (B vitamins, vitamin D, iron/ferritin, cobalt, magnesium, omega-3) and optimization targets.

Covers B-complex vitamin strategy including methylcobalamin vs. cyanocobalamin selection, MTHFR/COMT genetic variant implications, dosing timing (morning vs. evening), and lab-draw preparation protocols.
Instructs on vitamin D assessment, cofactor requirements for absorption (K2, magnesium), and distinction between low/normal/optimal serum levels.

Teaches comprehensive initial visit framework: 45–60 min intake, thyroid questionnaire scoring, targeted review-of-systems (fatigue, sleep, stress, palpitations, joint/muscle pain), and relevant ICD-10 diagnosis coding.
Provides lab ordering guidance including LabCorp/Quest account setup, electronic vs. hard-copy transmission, and insurance coverage justification using specific diagnosis codes.

Covers supplement quality assessment: FDA-approved facilities, third-party testing verification, ingredient transparency, avoidance of contaminants and heavy metals, and independent sealing standards.
Teaches nutrient-specific protocols: omega-3, berberine, curcumin, inositol (B8), biotin (B7) interference with 150+ lab processes, valerian root GABA mechanism, and magnesium application.

Instructs on clinical monitoring: glucose/insulin optimization, liver enzyme interpretation, protein/albumin assessment, and follow-up timing (Q3–4 months for iron/CMP until optimized; Q6–12 months for maintenance).
Teaches patient education essentials: distinguishing serving size from dose, label reading for duplicate ingredients, biotin cessation 5–7 days pre-lab draw, and supplement-medication interactions.

Addresses business model: positioning supplementation as standalone high-margin revenue stream suitable for wellness, anti-aging, HRT, functional medicine, aesthetics, primary care, and psychiatric practices.

Instructors include Justin Allan (FNP, $0–$70K/month practice model owner) and Jenni Gallagher (APRN, integrative/functional medicine owner), both running multi-service clinics incorporating supplement protocols.
Teaches metabolic/nutritional condition management: hypothyroidism coding, fatigue workup, morbid obesity, myalgia, anemia, and metabolic disease optimization through integrated nutrient protocols.

entries.title: Functional Psychiatry Case Analysis: Pediatric Depression with Family Suicide History
entries.pitch: Learn how to apply functional medicine frameworks to complex psychiatric cases involving genetic risk, medication concerns, and nutritional/lifestyle interventions in pediatric patients.
facts: Teaches functional assessment of pediatric depression including sleep disruption, social withdrawal, and academic decline as interconnected functional markers rather than isolated symptoms.
Covers family history analysis and genetic predisposition screening for mood disorders, suicide risk, and psychiatric inheritance patterns across generations.
Addresses the functional medicine approach to medication decisions, including understanding conventional drug therapy (SSRIs, hydroxyzine) alongside patient/parent concerns about black box warnings.
Teaches evaluation of nutritional and supplemental interventions (including trace minerals) as adjunctive or alternative options within a functional framework.
Includes assessment of sleep architecture dysfunction as a primary driver of mood and behavioral symptoms in children and adolescents.
Covers trauma and loss as functional stressors with physiological consequences, requiring systems-based intervention strategies.
Teaches how to elicit comprehensive environmental, lifestyle, and psychosocial data to identify root causes beyond diagnostic labels.
Demonstrates case-based reasoning for managing psychiatric cases where conventional treatment initiation raises patient/family safety or acceptance barriers.
Addresses the NP's role in coordinating functional interventions with conventional psychiatric care and PCP referrals.

entries.title: Functional Approach to Psychiatric Treatment
entries.pitch: Master functional medicine frameworks for depression, anxiety, ADHD, dementia, and insomnia—with evidence-based supplement protocols, lab interpretation, and private practice integration strategies.
facts: Teaches functional vs. integrative vs. orthomolecular approaches to mental health, grounded in systems biology and root-cause identification rather than symptom suppression alone.
Covers diagnostic and lab selection for mood disorders, anxiety, ADHD, PTSD, dementia, and insomnia—with guidance on when functional interventions are clinically safe and appropriate.

Trains NPs on nutritional and supplement protocols for depression (SAM-e, L-methylfolate, St. John's Wort, folate, lithium) and anxiety (magnesium glycinate, L-theanine, ashwagandha, kava, rhodiola rosea) with dosing frameworks.
Addresses hormone optimization for psychiatric symptoms—estrogen, progesterone, testosterone, thyroid, DHEA, and vitamin D—with specific guidance for perimenopausal and postmenopausal women.

Teaches comparative analysis of functional interventions vs. mainstream psychiatry, including standard of care, scientific basis, and when to collaborate with specialty psychiatry for bipolar disorder and suicidality.
Covers non-pharmacological in-office treatments including transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and ketamine, plus lifestyle interventions (exercise, diet, therapy, sleep optimization).

Includes specific clinical pearls for complex presentations: treatment-resistant depression, bipolar II (with safety warnings on SAM-e and St. John's Wort), ADHD elimination diets, and dementia lifestyle protocols.
Teaches risk assessment, informed consent, and patient education strategies for functional medicine—including placebo effects, provider bias, and cost/timeline realistic expectations.
Provides scope-of-practice guidance aligned with state nursing law, liability coverage, and collaboration thresholds for complex psychiatric conditions.
Demonstrates business integration strategies for incorporating functional elements into private practice to enhance patient experience and practice profitability.
Instructor Nicholas Goodwin, DNP, PMHNP brings clinical private practice experience teaching evidence-based and clinical-opinion-based functional psychiatry.
Covers special populations—young children, pregnant individuals, elderly—where functional approaches offer advantages due to pharmacological side-effect burden.

entries.title: Functional Hypothyroid Management
entries.pitch: Learn to interpret advanced thyroid panels, dose T3/T4 medications by symptom response rather than TSH, and address root nutritional and inflammatory drivers of thyroid dysfunction—a practice model that differentiates NPs in primary care.
facts: Teaches interpretation of six-marker thyroid panels (TSH, Free T4, Free T3, Reverse T3, TPO, TgAB) and why TSH alone is insufficient for functional management.
Covers the enzymatic conversion process from T4 to T3, deiodinase enzyme deficiencies, and MTHFR impact on thyroid hormone utilization.
Teaches clinical decision-making for choosing between levothyroxine (T4-only), liothyronine (T3), and natural desiccated thyroid (NDT) based on lab ratios and patient conversion capacity.
Provides dosing frameworks for liothyronine titration that mimic circadian thyroid hormone release (divided doses early AM, mid-morning, early afternoon) rather than single daily doses.
Covers essential pre-treatment screening for ferritin sufficiency (>45 ng/mL) before T3 dosing to prevent cardiac complications.
Teaches symptom-guided dosing protocols with safety monitoring (heart rate, blood pressure tracking on graphs) and recognition of hyperstimulation signs.
Addresses nutritional foundations required for thyroid function: iodine, vitamin D, iron, protein, and gut health/absorption capacity.
Covers lab follow-up timing (8–10 week intervals during titration, 6-month intervals long-term) and why in-person visits—not phone management—are required for T3 dosing safety.

Includes Hashimoto's-specific management: dietary inflammation elimination (grains, seed oils, dairy, oxalates), anti-inflammatory supplementation (vitamin C, black cumin, CoQ10, luteolin, berberine), and antibody monitoring.
Teaches comprehensive symptom assessment tools to identify thyroid dysfunction (fatigue, brain fog, hair loss, muscle pain, GI issues, mood changes, numbness/paresthesias).
Introduces adjunctive therapies like low-dose naltrexone (LDN) as non-first-line support after inflammation sources are eliminated.
Instructor is an APRN with real-world practice experience running a functional health clinic, using referenced protocols from *Recovering with T3*, *Hashimoto's Protocol*, and evidence-based blogs.
Teaches optimal lab ranges for medicated vs. unmedicated patients and how to interpret FT3/RT3 ratios to assess conversion efficiency and guide medication adjustments.

entries.title: Functional Medicine Pediatrics Course
entries.pitch: Master systems-based root cause identification and natural healing protocols for pediatric patients to build a high-demand cash-pay pediatric functional medicine practice.
facts: Teaches functional medicine framework applied to pediatric patients: identifying root causes (gut dysfunction, nutrient deficiencies, environmental toxins, emotional triggers) rather than symptom management alone.
Covers GI disorders comprehensively including constipation, stomachaches, and failure to thrive with both acute relief strategies and long-term gut healing protocols.
Instructs interpretation of pediatric-specific stool testing (GI MAP, Tiny Health for infants under 2) and microbiome analysis to guide dysbiosis treatment.
Teaches nutritional deficiency assessment and supplementation for common pediatric conditions: magnesium, B vitamins, lithium, vitamin D in mood and behavior disorders.
Addresses mood, behavior, anxiety, ADHD, and sleep disturbances through gut-brain connection lens with specific calming herbs, amino acids, and lifestyle interventions.
Covers food sensitivity elimination (dairy, gluten) and functional food sensitivity testing (KBMO Fit 176) as root cause investigation tools.
Teaches natural acute symptom relief techniques: castor oil packs, abdominal massage, herbal tinctures, homeopathy, craniosacral therapy referral protocols.
Includes real pediatric case studies (behavior concerns, failure to thrive, constipation) demonstrating diagnostic workup and 8-week to 2-month outcome tracking.

Instructors are active practitioners: Dr. Haley Stevens operates her own pediatric functional medicine practice; Justin Allan runs multiple cash-pay practices ($0-$70K monthly revenue model demonstrated).
Teaches cash-pay practice model positioning—emphasizes high demand for pediatric functional medicine providers and parental demand for alternative treatment options.
Covers integrated assessment: maternal diet analysis for breastfeeding infants, oral restrictions (tongue/lip tie), environmental toxin exposure, and family history genetics.
Teaches how to transition pediatric patients off unnecessary medications and diagnostic procedures through root cause restoration and natural healing protocols.

entries.title: Functional vs. Normal Lab Results: Optimized Reference Ranges & Interpretation
entries.pitch: Learn to interpret labs using functional medicine reference ranges rather than conventional normals—enabling earlier detection and prevention of chronic disease.
facts: Teaches optimal vitamin D ranges (60–100 ng/mL) versus mainstream reference ranges, with toxicity thresholds and associations to chronic disease.
Covers iron/ferritin optimization (80–120 range for both values) to assess oxygen transport and storage capacity beyond standard CBC interpretation.
Addresses thyroid optimization by teaching Free T3 ('gas pedal'), Reverse T3 ('brake pedal'), and TSH limitations—with specific optimal ranges (Free T3: 3.5–4 ng/dL; Reverse T3: 10–12 ng/dL).
Teaches glucose and HbA1c interpretation showing diabetes complications begin at 5.3% HbA1c, not the mainstream 7% threshold.
Includes continuous glucose monitor (CGM) use and fasting glucose targets (ideal in 80s) with OTC options (Stelo, Theia) for patient monitoring.
Covers fasting insulin optimization interpreted in context of A1C, fasting glucose, triglycerides, and thyroid status.
Teaches ferritin as inflammation marker when 1.5–2× higher than iron number; mineral testing via RBC (magnesium, chromium, selenium) not serum.
Addresses electrolyte optimization: sodium upper end of range (140 mEq/L), potassium upper half (4.0 mEq/L via RBC testing for accuracy).
Covers liver enzyme interpretation and protein fractions (albumin, globulin) linked to malnutrition and absorption.
Teaches hormone optimization: DHEAS mid-to-high range, total testosterone mid-range or higher, free testosterone upper 1/3, estradiol near 100 pg/mL, estrone as low as possible.
Includes inflammation marker panel interpretation (CRP-HS, WBC, homocysteine, uric acid, TPO/TgAb, other autoimmune markers) for root-cause assessment.
Taught by Jenni Gallagher, APRN, functional medicine practitioner at Joyful Heart Healthcare, grounded in peer-reviewed cardiovascular and metabolic research.
Emphasizes paradigm shift from symptom management to optimization: more patient time, food/nutrient/lifestyle focus versus prescription-heavy mainstream care.

entries.title: Gut Health Module
entries.pitch: Master functional assessment of the entire digestive tract, identify root causes of GI dysfunction, and apply evidence-based treatment protocols for common conditions like SIBO, dysbiosis, and H. pylori.
facts: Teaches systematic functional anatomy of digestion from mastication through large intestine, linking each stage to common pathologies and absorption barriers.
Covers Bristol Stool Form Scale assessment and teaches how to screen for chronic constipation using a 15-question symptom checklist to catch subtle dysfunction.
Trains interpretation of advanced stool testing panels including OCP, C&S, C. difficile, FOBT/FIT, fecal calprotectin, lactoferrin, secretory IgA, and zonulin.
Addresses 15+ comorbidities connected to digestive health including metabolic syndrome, autoimmune disease, NAFLD, mental health, Parkinson's, and Alzheimer's.
Teaches diagnosis and treatment protocols for SIBO, candida overgrowth, parasites, H. pylori, and celiac disease with both pharmaceutical and botanical options.
Covers how medications (PPIs, H2 blockers) impair absorption of sodium, chloride, fats, and vitamin A, and teaches nutrient repletion strategies.
Teaches differential use of specific probiotic strains (Lactobacillus acidophilus, reuteri, rhamnosus; Bifidobacterium bifidum; Saccharomyces boulardii) for H. pylori eradication.
Trains interpretation of comprehensive stool labs from major companies (GI Map, Doctor's Data, Genova) using a holistic framework that integrates symptoms, serum labs, medications, and supplements.
Covers botanical and antimicrobial treatment options for dysbiosis and intestinal permeability including oregano, barberry, goldenseal, garlic, and combination protocols.
Instructs how to assess for nutrient deficiencies (iron, trace minerals, electrolytes) in celiac disease and design repair protocols including digestive enzyme support.
Teaches how to avoid over-focusing on test minutiae and instead synthesize overall clinical picture for functional GI assessment and treatment planning.
Taught by Jenni Gallagher, APRN, Program Director for Elite NP's Functional Medicine Certification with evidence-based references from peer-reviewed nutrition and gastroenterology literature.

entries.title: Infectious Disease in Functional Medicine: Lyme, EBV & Long Haul COVID-19
entries.pitch: Master pathophysiology, targeted lab interpretation, and foundational management protocols for three major post-infectious conditions your NP patients are asking about.
facts: Teaches pathophysiology of Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi transmission, dissemination), EBV (B-lymphocyte infection, latency), and Long Haul COVID-19 (ACE2 receptor mechanisms, multi-organ impacts across 10 disease categories).

Covers specific lab panels for diagnosis: Lyme ELISA with reflex antibody testing (includes LabCorp and Quest test codes), EBV serology interpretation (Early Antigen, Viral Capsid Antigen, Nuclear Antigen antibodies), and quantitative/semi-quantitative SARS-CoV2 antibody testing.

Teaches assessment frameworks including comprehensive review of systems, symptom questionnaires (with access to validated research instruments and instructor-developed tools), cardiac function evaluation, and multi-system screening protocols.

Addresses differential and supportive lab interpretation: CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel, vitamin D, thyroid panel (TSH, FT4, FT3, reverse T3), homocysteine, iron studies, hormone panels, high-sensitivity CRP, and B12/folate status.

Covers foundational management approaches including antibiotic trial decision-making for Lyme/Long Haul COVID, immunomodulatory options (IV immunoglobulin, low-dose naltrexone, steroids), and antivirals for herpes reactivation.

Teaches anti-inflammatory protocol selection with specific supplement categories: Vitamin D with cofactors, omega-3 fish oil, curcumin, quercetin, NAC, turkey tail mushroom, resveratrol, glutathione precursors, CoQ10, and melatonin.

Includes multi-system treatment considerations for comorbid Lyme and Long Haul COVID, addressing inflammation, immune support, and duration of therapy (2-3 month treatment windows with dosing titration).

Teaches sleep and recovery support strategies: low-dose naltrexone, progesterone for females, melatonin, GABA, L-theanine, valerian, and lifestyle interventions (walking, blue light management, sleep hygiene).
Covers treatment decision-making framework using patient symptom reports and lab results to guide protocol selection, with emphasis on globulin optimization (target 2.9-3.3 g/dL) for immune health.
Includes follow-up and monitoring protocols: repeat labs every 4-6 months, symptom questionnaire reassessment every 6 months, and treatment duration guidance based on clinical response.
Instructor is Jenni Gallagher, APRN, with clinical practice background in Nebraska, emphasizing evidence-based decision-making with individual patient customization.
Addresses real-world clinical challenges: half of Lyme patients lack detectable antibodies, 2/3 of patients respond to antibiotic trials, and 70% of chronic Lyme resolve with appropriate therapy.

entries.title: Iron Optimization & Energy/Hair Growth Module
entries.pitch: Learn to distinguish iron deficiency from hypothyroidism using functional lab interpretation and evidence-based supplementation strategies to resolve fatigue and hair loss in clinical practice.
facts: Teaches differentiation between low iron, low ferritin, and hypothyroidism—which present with identical symptoms (fatigue, hair loss, brain fog) but require different treatment approaches.
Covers functional vs. conventional lab ranges for ferritin (optimal 80–100 ng/mL) and explains symptom progression at each deficiency stage (65, 45, 20 ng/mL thresholds).
Instructs on iron absorption cofactors including vitamin C, vitamin D, trace minerals (copper, zinc, selenium, manganese, molybdenum), and dietary factors that enhance or block iron uptake.
Teaches oral supplementation protocols including Ferrochel dosing, high-dose vitamin C ratios, and dietary interventions (red meat emphasis, grain elimination rationale).
Covers IV iron infusion indications, ordering procedures, and facility-specific protocols (Feraheme and Venofer dosing/frequency) when oral supplementation fails or insurance barriers exist.
Instructs safety protocols including iron toxicity monitoring, contraindication of liothyronine when ferritin <45, and cardiac risk stratification at critical ferritin thresholds.
Teaches comprehensive follow-up laboratory schedules (Q4 months during treatment, Q6–12 months post-discontinuation) and patient education on long-term monitoring without continuous supplementation.
Covers ICD-10 coding for fatigue, myalgia, metabolic/endocrine/nutritional disorders, and hypothyroidism to support billing and documentation in functional medicine practice.
Addresses anemia type differentiation (iron deficiency anemia, B12 anemia, anemia of chronic disease) and their distinct lab implications for NP diagnostic decision-making.
